title: Continuous telemetry enables linkage of multiple observations to the same wearer
description: Heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps collected continuously by the wearable can be correlated over time, allowing records and sessions to be linked to one wearer and to each other, revealing routines and identity-related patterns.
assumptions: The device stores or transmits telemetry with a persistent device identifier, account binding, or otherwise stable context over time.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for linkability; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary.

title: Telemetry content can identify the wearer
description: Fine-grained GPS traces, timestamps, activity patterns, and biometrics such as heart rate can directly or indirectly identify the wearer by exposing home/work locations, habitual routes, and unique physiological or behavioral signatures.
assumptions: Telemetry is available in sufficient granularity to single out an individual or is associated with other identifying context.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for identifiability; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary.

title: Sensitive information is disclosed through raw health and location telemetry
description: The flow includes potentially sensitive personal data such as health-related measurements, precise location, and time information. If exposed beyond what is necessary, it can disclose health status, movements, habits, and other intimate details about the wearer.
assumptions: The wearable or connected ecosystem may expose, retain, or share raw telemetry beyond the immediate sensing purpose.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for information disclosure / excessive disclosure; exact subtree may differ.

title: Continuous sensing allows inference of private habits and states
description: Even if explicit conclusions are not collected directly, combining timestamps, GPS, heart rate, and step data allows derivation of sleep patterns, exercise routines, workplace, home address, religious attendance, medical conditions, or other sensitive lifestyle attributes.
assumptions: The device or downstream systems analyze or can analyze telemetry over time.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for detectability/inference-style threat; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ because this borders on derived disclosure.

title: The wearer may be unaware of the extent and granularity of continuous collection
description: Because sensing is continuous and multi-modal, the wearer may not fully understand when data is captured, what exact data types are collected, how precise location/time traces are, or how long the telemetry is retained or used.
assumptions: The device does not provide sufficiently clear, timely, and granular notice about ongoing collection.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for unawareness / insufficient notice; exact subtree may vary.

title: Collection may exceed what is necessary for the stated purpose or valid consent
description: Continuous capture of heart rate, steps, GPS, and timestamps may not be necessary at full frequency or precision for all intended functions. If purpose limitation, data minimization, or valid consent is not established, the flow may be non-compliant with privacy obligations.
assumptions: Not all collected fields or collection frequency are strictly necessary for the primary service, or lawful basis/consent is incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for non-compliance / unlawful or excessive collection; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: The wearer may later be unable to prove or dispute what telemetry was provided
description: If the system lacks reliable receipts, logs, or user-visible records of what data was captured and when, the wearer may be unable to repudiate or contest claims about submitted telemetry, such as whether location or health readings were actually collected at a certain time.
assumptions: There is no user-accessible audit trail or trustworthy evidence mechanism for the capture events.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for non-repudiation-related privacy threat; applicability depends on whether disputes over captured telemetry are in scope.

title: Linkability of sensor batches across sessions via persistent device identifier
description: The companion app receives a persistent device identifier together with exercise sessions, GPS traces, and timestamps. This can allow records from multiple syncs and sessions to be linked to the same wearer over time, enabling construction of a long-term activity profile.
assumptions: The device identifier is stable across syncs and stored or used by the app.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability via persistent identifiers; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode naming may vary.

title: Identifiability of the wearer from GPS traces and device identifier
description: GPS traces for exercise sessions, combined with timestamps and a device identifier, can directly or indirectly identify the individual wearer by revealing home/work locations, routines, or by tying data to a known device/account.
assumptions: The app can access raw GPS traces and associate them with a user account or other identifying context.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability from directly identifying or quasi-identifying data; exact subnode id may differ in some LINDDUN Pro catalogs.

title: Disclosure of sensitive activity and location data during device-to-app sync
description: Exercise sessions, fine-grained GPS traces, timestamps, and device identifiers are privacy-sensitive. If the sync channel or receiving app context is insufficiently protected, an attacker or unauthorized party could observe or access the transmitted data.
assumptions: There is some opportunity for interception, unauthorized local access, insecure logging, or over-broad app access on the phone.
uncertainty_note: Mapped to a general disclosure/interception-at-data-flow style node; exact node id may differ.

title: Detectability of user activity patterns from periodic sync traffic
description: Even if payload contents are protected, the presence, timing, size, or frequency of syncs from the wearable to the app may reveal that the user has been exercising, when sessions occur, or roughly how much data was collected.
assumptions: An observer can see sync events or metadata such as Bluetooth traffic timing/volume.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability node for inferring sensitive events from communication metadata; exact subnode id may vary.

title: Collection and transfer of more sensor and location data than necessary
description: The flow includes detailed exercise sessions, GPS traces, device id, and timestamps. If all of these fields are not strictly necessary for the app's stated purpose, the sync may violate data minimization or purpose limitation expectations.
assumptions: Some features of the companion app may not require raw or persistent versions of all transmitted fields.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance/privacy principle violation node; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Users may be unaware of the granularity and sensitivity of synced data
description: The wearer may not understand that the device sync includes detailed GPS traces, timestamps, and persistent device identifiers, preventing informed consent or meaningful control over the privacy impact of the transfer.
assumptions: The wearable/app ecosystem does not clearly communicate what is synced and at what granularity.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness node; exact subnode id may differ.

title: Disclosure of highly sensitive health and lifestyle data entered by the user
description: The flow carries calorie intake, meal details, and weight entries from the user to the companion app. If this data is exposed in transit within the device UI/input pipeline, app logs, crash reports, screenshots, clipboard integrations, or insecure local handling on receipt, an attacker or unauthorized party could learn sensitive health, diet, and lifestyle information about the user.
assumptions: The companion app processes and may temporarily store submitted entries; mobile platform or app components could expose entered data beyond the intended purpose if not properly protected.
uncertainty_note: The exact LINDDUN Pro node id may vary by catalog version; D.1.1 is my best fit for data disclosure on a data flow/receipt context.

title: Identifiability of the user from nutrition and weight logs
description: Meal patterns, calorie intake, and weight history can act as quasi-identifiers. When combined with account information, device identifiers, timestamps, or other app data, the received entries may allow the wearer to be identified or singled out.
assumptions: The app can associate submissions with an account, device, or persistent profile.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability; exact numbering may differ across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Linkability of separate food and weight entries over time
description: Repeated manual logs received by the app can be linked together by account, device, timestamps, or behavioral patterns, enabling construction of a longitudinal profile of eating habits and weight change. This permits linking otherwise separate events to the same individual.
assumptions: Entries are associated with a stable user account or persistent app instance.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for linkability of records/events within one service.

title: User cannot plausibly deny having submitted specific diet or weight entries
description: If the app records timestamps, account bindings, synchronization metadata, or audit trails when the user logs data, those records may later be used to prove that the user submitted specific meals or weight values. This creates a non-repudiation risk for sensitive self-reported health information.
assumptions: The app maintains persistent records or audit metadata tied to the user identity.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering for non-repudiation may differ.

title: Unawareness of the sensitivity and downstream use of entered data
description: The wearer may not realize that manually entered calorie, meal, and weight data can be inferred into health status, eating behavior, or other sensitive attributes, or that the app may retain, analyze, sync, or share it beyond immediate display. Insufficient notice at data entry time can leave the user unaware of collection scope and consequences.
assumptions: The app may not provide clear, contextual privacy notice or granular controls at the moment of data entry.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency; exact numbering may differ.

title: Collection or processing of diet and weight data without valid, informed consent or other lawful basis
description: Calorie intake, meals, and weight entries may constitute health-related or otherwise sensitive personal data depending on jurisdiction and context. If the app collects and processes this information without explicit informed consent, adequate notice, or another valid legal basis, the flow creates a non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Applicable law or policy treats these entries as personal or sensitive data and requires specific transparency, consent, minimization, or purpose-limitation measures.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for consent/lawfulness/compliance issues in LINDDUN Pro; exact numbering may vary.

title: Stored health logs can directly identify the user
description: The health log store contains calorie intake, weight history, and exercise sessions tied to an app account or device context. If records are stored with direct identifiers such as user account ID, email address, or stable device identifier, the data in this flow can be used to identify a specific individual.
assumptions: Assumes health log entries are written with a persistent user or device identifier so the store can associate logs with one person over time.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is my best-fit estimate for identifiability via direct identifiers in stored data.

title: Health log records are linkable across time
description: Repeated writes of weight history, calorie intake, and exercise sessions enable the datastore to link multiple events to the same person and build a longitudinal behavioral profile. Even if each entry seems harmless alone, the combined history increases linkability.
assumptions: Assumes the datastore uses a persistent key, account identifier, or other stable reference to append new logs to the same subject record.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability of multiple records belonging to the same data subject over time.

title: Sensitive lifestyle and health attributes can be inferred from stored logs
description: Calorie intake, weight changes, and exercise patterns can reveal sensitive information such as obesity status, dieting behavior, pregnancy-related changes, injuries, chronic conditions, or religious/cultural habits. Writing these logs to the store creates a repository from which such inferences may be drawn.
assumptions: Assumes analysts, internal services, or attackers with access to DS1 can examine the stored data and derive higher-level conclusions.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an estimated best fit for inference from observed personal data.

title: Detailed history reveals highly granular personal behavior
description: The datastore accumulates fine-grained histories of eating, exercise, and weight over time. This level of detail may exceed what users expect to be stored and can expose day-to-day routines, habits, and progress with substantial precision.
assumptions: Assumes the flow writes individual events or measurements rather than only coarse summaries, and that retention preserves this granularity.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for excessive detectability/discoverability due to detailed stored personal data; exact subtree may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: User may be unable to deny submission of specific health logs
description: If the app writes health logs with timestamps, account identifiers, and audit metadata, those records may later be used as evidence that the user submitted particular weight, calorie, or exercise entries. This creates a non-repudiation risk from a privacy perspective.
assumptions: Assumes the system retains write timestamps, device/account identifiers, or audit trails linking submissions to the user.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit estimate for privacy-relevant non-repudiation caused by logged submissions.

title: Purpose of storing health logs may be unclear to users
description: Users may not understand why detailed calorie, weight, and exercise logs are written to persistent storage, how long they are retained, or which internal features use them. This can undermine user awareness and informed expectations about the processing.
assumptions: Assumes the app does not clearly explain storage purpose, retention, and downstream use at the point logs are captured and written.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an estimated best fit for lack of user awareness/transparency.

title: Storage of health logs may exceed consent or user expectations
description: Persistently storing detailed health logs may be incompatible with the user's granted consent if consent was absent, bundled, or limited to immediate app functionality rather than long-term retention or secondary use. Health-related data is especially sensitive, increasing the compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes consent, necessity, or another lawful basis may not clearly cover long-term storage and possible secondary processing of these logs.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit estimate for non-compliance related to consent/lawful basis and storage limitation; exact node naming may differ across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Stored location traces enable linkage across sessions and contexts
description: GPS traces with timestamps written into the location history store can be linked over time to the same device or account, allowing records from different trips, days, or app uses to be associated and revealing persistent behavioral patterns.
assumptions: The store retains identifiers or stable pseudonyms, or otherwise allows records to be associated with the same user/device over time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

title: Location history identifies the user through unique mobility patterns
description: Even if direct identifiers are omitted, fine-grained GPS traces with timestamps are often unique enough to identify an individual by home/work locations, routine paths, or correlation with external knowledge.
assumptions: Location precision and retention are sufficient to reveal recurring places or trajectories.
uncertainty_note: Node id is my best estimate; identification sub-node naming may vary.

title: Location history exposes precise whereabouts and routines
description: The stored data reveals sensitive personal information such as places visited, travel habits, daily routines, and potentially special-category inferences like visits to clinics, places of worship, or political events.
assumptions: The store contains sufficiently precise coordinates and timestamps and is accessible to internal components, analysts, or attackers beyond the minimum need.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node from memory; exact subtree may differ.

title: Long-term storage enables broader data dissemination than expected
description: Persisting raw location traces in a history store increases the chance that the data is shared, queried, repurposed, or transferred to additional parties or systems beyond the user's expectations, expanding exposure over time.
assumptions: Other services, staff, analytics pipelines, or third parties may access or receive data from the store.
uncertainty_note: Dissemination node id is approximate; threat applicability depends on downstream sharing not described explicitly in the flow.

title: Users may be unaware that detailed movement history is being retained
description: Writing GPS traces with timestamps to a dedicated history store may be non-transparent to users, especially if retention period, granularity, or secondary uses are not clearly communicated in the app experience.
assumptions: The app does not fully explain collection frequency, retention, and use of historical location data at the point of collection.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/unawareness node from memory; exact node label may differ.

title: Location history storage may exceed consented purpose or legal basis
description: Storing detailed GPS traces with timestamps can violate data minimization, purpose limitation, storage limitation, or consent requirements if the app collects more precision or retains data longer than necessary for its stated purpose.
assumptions: Applicable privacy requirements constrain precision, retention, or purpose, and these controls may be absent or insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance subtree id is approximate because no specific jurisdiction or stated purpose is provided.

title: Cross-session linkage of health logs to the same individual
description: The analytics service reads calorie, weight, and exercise logs across sessions, enabling records from different times and contexts to be linked to one person or account for longitudinal analysis. This may expose behavior patterns and make otherwise separate observations correlatable.
assumptions: Health logs are associated with a stable account, device identifier, or pseudonymous user key that persists across sessions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary depending on whether the model treats this primarily as linkability of messages/records or linkability of identities.

title: Inference of sensitive health condition from combined logs
description: By analyzing calorie intake, weight trends, and exercise patterns together over time, the service may infer sensitive information such as medical conditions, pregnancy, eating disorders, disability, recovery state, or other health-related attributes beyond what the user explicitly disclosed.
assumptions: Analytics includes trend detection, segmentation, profiling, or model-based analysis rather than simple aggregation only.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for inference from data analysis; exact subnode naming may differ in a specific LINDDUN Pro catalog.

title: Exposure of identifiable health logs to the analytics service
description: The data flow may provide the analytics service with directly or indirectly identifiable calorie, weight, and exercise logs. Because these are sensitive health-related records, unnecessary access, broad query scope, or insufficient separation from identifiers can disclose personal information to the receiving process.
assumptions: The service can access user-linked records rather than only fully anonymized aggregates.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node; exact subnode may depend on whether the emphasis is on content disclosure, identifier disclosure, or excessive collection/access.

title: Insufficient unawareness about secondary analytics use of health logs
description: Individuals may not realize that logs originally entered for tracking diet, weight, or exercise are later read across sessions for health-condition analysis. If this secondary use is not clearly communicated, users can be unaware of the extent, purpose, or sensitivity of the analysis performed on their stored data.
assumptions: Not all users were explicitly informed that stored logs would be reused for health-condition analytics beyond immediate journaling/tracking.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/unawareness-related node id; exact LINDDUN Pro mapping for unawareness subnodes may differ.

title: Processing of sensitive health-related logs beyond compatible purpose or legal basis
description: Reading stored calorie, weight, and exercise logs across sessions for health-condition analysis may exceed the original collection purpose or require additional consent/legal basis due to the sensitive nature of inferred health data. This creates a risk of non-compliance with purpose limitation, transparency, data minimization, or special-category data requirements.
assumptions: The original purpose presented to users may have been simple logging or wellness tracking rather than health-condition analysis.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate because LINDDUN Pro non-compliance subtrees vary by legal/control objective.

title: Cross-session location history enables linkage of user activity over time
description: By querying location history across sessions, the analytics service can link records that belong to the same individual over multiple time periods, creating a longitudinal view of movements and routines.
assumptions: Location history records are associated with a stable user, device, or account identifier that the analytics service can use across sessions.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen as a best-fit for linkability via correlation of records across sessions; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary by threat-tree version.

title: Daily routine and movement patterns may identify an individual
description: Deriving home/work locations, commute patterns, and habitual visits from location history can make a person directly or indirectly identifiable, even if explicit identifiers are absent.
assumptions: The analytics outputs or queried raw history include sufficiently granular time/location points to infer distinctive routines.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability from data content/inference; exact subnode may differ across LINDDUN Pro editions.

title: Routine analysis discloses sensitive behavioral patterns
description: Analysis of historical locations can reveal sensitive information such as visits to clinics, religious venues, political events, or other intimate aspects of a person's life through inferred movement patterns.
assumptions: Location history has enough spatial/temporal precision to infer visits to sensitive places or recurring behaviors.
uncertainty_note: Selected as a disclosure-of-information best fit for sensitive data inference from location histories; exact node id may differ.

title: Analytics infers habits and future movements from historical location data
description: The service derives daily routines and movement patterns from accumulated location history, enabling profiling and inference of habits, preferences, and likely future whereabouts beyond the original raw observations.
assumptions: The analytics service stores or acts upon inferred profiles or pattern models derived from the queried history.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is a best-fit for detectability/profiling-style inference from accumulated data; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary.

title: Secondary use of location history for behavioral analytics may exceed original purpose
description: Using stored location history across sessions to derive routines and movement patterns may be incompatible with the purpose originally communicated when the data was collected, creating a policy/consent compliance risk.
assumptions: The original notice, consent, or legal basis for collecting location history did not explicitly cover longitudinal behavioral analytics.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node for purpose limitation/consent mismatch; exact node id may differ by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Exposure of sensitive inferred health insights in transit to the mobile app
description: The analytics service sends inferred health-condition risk indicators, routine summaries, and trend flags to the companion app. If the flow is insufficiently protected or routed through components with broad access, these inferences may be disclosed to unauthorized parties. Because the data consists of derived health insights, disclosure could reveal highly sensitive medical or behavioral information beyond the raw input data.
assumptions: The flow traverses a network or intermediary stack where transport, endpoint, or logging protections may be imperfect.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro disclosure subtree label may differ.

title: Linkability of inferred insights to a specific user's broader activity history
description: Repeated delivery of risk indicators and trend summaries to the app can enable linking multiple observations over time to the same individual or device. Even if individual messages are pseudonymous internally, stable identifiers, session metadata, or distinctive health-inference patterns may allow the app context or observers to correlate records across time and reconstruct a detailed profile.
assumptions: The app or surrounding ecosystem uses stable account, device, or session identifiers, or the content itself is distinctive enough to support correlation.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate; exact linkability subtree numbering may vary.

title: Identifiability of the user from personalized health analytics output
description: The returned insights are individualized and may contain rare combinations of condition-risk signals, routines, or trends that single out a person. If exposed on-device, in notifications, screenshots, telemetry, or support logs, the output may make the user directly or indirectly identifiable even without explicit identifiers in the payload.
assumptions: The analytics output is sufficiently personalized or granular to distinguish one user from others.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort tree node id; exact identifiability node mapping may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Over-collection and over-sharing of inferred health data to the app
description: The analytics service may return more inferred information than is necessary for the app feature, such as detailed risk indicators, longitudinal summaries, or extra trend attributes not required for the immediate user interaction. Sharing excessive derived health information increases privacy impact and downstream exposure.
assumptions: The app could fulfill its purpose with less granular, less frequent, or more localized summaries than are currently returned.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is a best-fit estimate for data minimization / unnecessary disclosure; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Users may be unaware that sensitive health inferences are generated and sent to the app
description: The flow delivers derived risk indicators and trend flags that may not be obvious to the user from their original inputs. If the system does not clearly explain that analytics produces and transmits such inferences, users may not understand the nature, sensitivity, or implications of the processing.
assumptions: Transparency notices, in-product explanations, or just-in-time disclosures may be limited or hard to understand.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate fit for lack of awareness / insufficient transparency.

title: Inferred health analytics may be processed or shared without valid consent or other lawful basis
description: Health-condition risk indicators and related trend inferences are likely sensitive personal data. Returning them to the app for display or further use may exceed the scope of the user's consent or another applicable legal basis, especially if the user agreed only to basic tracking rather than generation of health-risk inferences.
assumptions: The legal basis for generating and communicating inferred health insights is narrower than for collecting raw wellness data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node id from memory; exact legal-basis/consent subtree numbering may differ.

title: Lack of evidence about whether the user received, viewed, or acted on sensitive inferences
description: If the system does not maintain appropriate records of delivery, presentation, or acknowledgement of important inferred health insights, parties may later dispute whether a risk indicator or trend flag was actually communicated. This can create accountability issues around sensitive privacy-affecting outputs.
assumptions: The product relies on delivery or acknowledgement of analytics insights for support, safety follow-up, or user-rights handling.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on whether proof of communication matters in this context; node id is approximate.

title: Dashboard reveals sensitive inferred health status to anyone viewing the screen
description: The app presents trends and inferred eating-disorder or diabetes risk indicators. If the display is visible to people nearby, shown during screen sharing, or exposed through screenshots/notifications, sensitive health-related information can be disclosed to unintended recipients.
assumptions: The mobile app shows the indicators in clear form on-screen and the user may access the dashboard in contexts where others can observe the device.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id based on general LINDDUN knowledge; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree label for visual/on-screen disclosure may differ.

title: Highly sensitive inferences are exposed in identifiable form to the user endpoint
description: The flow communicates inferred condition indicators tied to a specific wearer account. These inferences may be stored in app UI state, caches, logs, analytics events, screenshots, or OS-level recent-app views, increasing the chance that identity-linked sensitive health inferences are exposed beyond the intended moment of display.
assumptions: The app or mobile OS may retain UI content, logs, thumbnails, or analytics metadata associated with the displayed dashboard.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for identifiability-related exposure in a display flow; exact Pro node may differ.

title: User may be unaware that indicators are inferred predictions rather than confirmed diagnoses
description: If the dashboard does not clearly explain that the shown eating-disorder or diabetes signals are algorithmic inferences with uncertainty, the wearer may misunderstand what personal data is being derived and disclosed, undermining transparency.
assumptions: The UI may emphasize scores or warnings without adequate explanation of derivation, confidence, or limitations.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of user awareness/transparency; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Displaying inferred condition indicators may exceed the user's expected consent scope
description: Even though the information is shown back to the wearer, presenting sensitive inferred health-risk indicators can constitute processing of special-category data. If the user did not explicitly consent to generation and presentation of such inferences, this flow may violate consent and purpose expectations.
assumptions: Consent may have covered wellness tracking generally but not sensitive condition inference or risk scoring presentation.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for consent/purpose non-compliance from general LINDDUN knowledge; exact Pro node id may differ.

title: Lack of evidence about what sensitive result was shown and when
description: If there is no trustworthy record of which inferred indicators were displayed, with what explanation and at what time, the organization may be unable to demonstrate that the user was properly informed or to resolve disputes about whether alarming or sensitive results were presented.
assumptions: The system may not keep auditable records of dashboard content/versioning or user acknowledgment for sensitive inferences.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is a weaker fit for this user-display flow, so applicability is lower than disclosure/transparency threats.

title: Third-party cloud hosting exposes highly sensitive health and location data to an additional party
description: The full health and location dataset, analytics outputs, and models are hosted and replicated at the cloud provider, making the provider a distinct recipient that can access or process special-category health data and precise location data beyond the originating analytics service.
assumptions: The cloud provider can technically access hosted content through infrastructure, administration, support, backup, or lawful access processes.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro disclosure subtree label may differ.

title: Cross-dataset linking by the cloud provider can re-identify individuals
description: Because the hosted content includes the full health and location dataset together with analytics data and models, the cloud provider may be able to correlate records across datasets, backups, logs, or tenant metadata to link records to the same individual and strengthen identifiability.
assumptions: The provider has visibility into stored datasets, metadata, or operational logs sufficient to correlate records.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an informed estimate; exact linkability subtree id may differ.

title: Cloud-side metadata and storage context can enable identification of data subjects
description: Even if direct identifiers are minimized in analytics outputs, the combination of full health data, location traces, account metadata, bucket names, access logs, timestamps, and tenancy information at the cloud provider may permit identifying individual data subjects.
assumptions: Operational metadata is retained by the provider and can be associated with the hosted datasets.
uncertainty_note: Exact identifiability node id may differ; chosen as best-fit from memory.

title: Replication and backup copies broaden disclosure surface
description: Replication of the hosted datasets to additional regions, storage tiers, backups, or disaster-recovery systems increases the number of copies and access paths through which health and location data could be disclosed.
assumptions: Replication includes additional storage locations or operational copies managed by the provider.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure-related node id from memory; exact subtree id may differ.

title: Individuals may be unaware that their full dataset is stored and replicated by a cloud provider
description: Data subjects may not realize that their health and location data, analytics outputs, and models are transferred to and replicated within a third-party cloud environment, reducing transparency about who processes their data and where it is stored.
assumptions: User-facing notices do not clearly explain third-party hosting, replication, and related processing roles.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness node id from memory; exact label may differ.

title: Third-party hosting and replication may be incompatible with consent, purpose limitation, or data minimization expectations
description: Hosting the full health and location dataset and derived models at an external cloud provider may exceed the purposes, jurisdictions, retention periods, or processor arrangements originally communicated to data subjects, creating non-compliance risk.
assumptions: The system lacks explicit legal basis, contractual safeguards, or transparent notices covering cloud hosting, replication, and any cross-border processing.
uncertainty_note: Exact non-compliance subtree id may differ; this is a best-fit classification.
